cli.input: --input selects the checkpoint registry only; default /app/data/checkpoint_registry.json

description: Output contract for the resume planner. Shapes, paths, field lists and sort orders only; no derivation rule lives here.

field_notes.rank_count: how many distinct ranks those entries cover
field_notes.shard_count: how many registry entries the checkpoint at that step carries, model and optimizer shards together
field_notes.total_bytes: the sum of the bytes those entries report

refetch_queue.fields_are_exclusive: the listed fields are the whole record: it carries these and no others, the same way the output directory carries exactly the three named files
refetch_queue.serialisation: one compact JSON object per line, trailing newline

resume_plan.fields_are_exclusive: the listed fields are the whole record: it carries these and no others, the same way the output directory carries exactly the three named files
resume_plan.serialisation: JSON object, two-space indent, trailing newline
resume_plan.sort: checkpoints ascending by step; refetch in the admitted order

field_notes.admissible_checkpoint_count: of those complete steps, the ones written strictly before the first poisoned step, so a complete checkpoint the run poisoned is counted by complete_checkpoint_count and not by this
field_notes.checkpoint_count: distinct steps those records name, complete or not
field_notes.complete_checkpoint_count: steps carrying a model and an optimizer shard for EVERY rank in the effective world size; poisoning is not considered here
field_notes.effective_world_size/effective_refetch_b: the values in force once the policy is resolved, whether from the policy file or from the governed baseline
field_notes.entry_count: records in the registry handed to --input
field_notes.first_poisoned_step: the first step of the earliest poisoned epoch, or -1 when the incident poisons no epoch
field_notes.refetch_deferred_count: of those, the ones deferred; needed is always planned plus deferred
field_notes.refetch_needed_count: shards needing refetch before the resume, before the budget and the cap
field_notes.refetch_planned_bytes: stored bytes of the planned refetches only, not of the deferred
field_notes.refetch_planned_count: of those, the ones the budget and the cap admit into the plan
field_notes.resume_step: the highest admissible step, or -1 when none is admissible

summary.fields_are_exclusive: the listed fields are the whole record: it carries these and no others, the same way the output directory carries exactly the three named files
summary.serialisation: JSON object, two-space indent, trailing newline

checkpoint_registry.fields_are_exclusive: the listed fields are the whole record: it carries these and no others, the same way the output directory carries exactly the three named files
checkpoint_registry.serialisation: JSON array, two-space indent, trailing newline
checkpoint_registry.sort: ascending by step, then rank, then kind, then entry_id

units.byte_range: every byte figure is a signed 64-bit integer and may carry any value from 0 to 9223372036854775807: a shard's bytes, a checkpoint's total_bytes, the policy's refetch_budget_bytes and refetch_planned_bytes alike. The budget is a mathematical bound. A shard is admitted only where the planned total including it is genuinely no greater than the budget, so a running total that would pass the ceiling defers the shard rather than admitting it on a wrapped comparison
units.step: optimizer steps since the run began
